title: Tissue/tumor segmentation task (CC0 Camelyon control)
context: Camelyon16/17 (lymph-node metastasis detection in WSIs) is released under CC0, making it suitable as a control task where derived artifacts can also be released CC0. Adding a tissue or tumor segmentation task using the Camelyon data allows the benchmark to test a different problem structure (pixel/patch-level segmentation vs slide-level classification) and provides a freely redistributable derived dataset. The CC0 license must be verified for current Camelyon terms before any ingest. The full license gate + de-id re-scan still applies. Domain-reviewer sign-off required on the task definition and splits.
objective: Define and produce a tissue/tumor segmentation benchmark task using Camelyon16 or Camelyon17 (CC0): verify the current CC0 license terms, add an approved allow-list entry, run the de-id re-scan on the ingested slides, tile and produce segmentation masks following the standard pipeline, define a segmentation task spec (inputs, label definition, metric e.g. FROC or AUROC at the patch/slide level), produce leakage-safe splits, and commit derived artifacts under CC0 where the license confirms CC0 derivability.
acceptanceCriteria: Current Camelyon16/17 CC0 license terms are verified and an approved allow-list entry with license: CC0 is committed in sources/allowlist.yml.
De-id re-scan is run on the Camelyon batch (100% screened); any positive is quarantined; a quarantine report is published.
A segmentation task spec is defined: inputs, label definition (tumor mask provenance), allowed data, and primary metric (e.g. FROC or AUROC).
Leakage-safe, patient-grouped splits are produced (site stratification applied where Camelyon data has multi-site structure).
Derived artifacts (tiles, masks) are committed or referenced under CC0 where the Camelyon license confirms CC0 derivability.
A datasheet for the Camelyon-derived dataset carries the 'not for clinical or diagnostic use; research only' notice.
Domain-reviewer and license-reviewer sign-off are recorded in the governance log.
output: A tissue/tumor segmentation task dataset (Camelyon, CC0) with verified license, de-id report, task spec, splits, datasheet, and domain-reviewer sign-off, committed via PR.
